steps.title: Acclimate mouse on treadmill
steps.instruction: Gently place the mouse on the stationary belt with the enclosure door closed and allow it to explore and calm for 1–2 minutes before any belt movement.

steps.title: Start treadmill and reach steady state
steps.instruction: Start the treadmill at 10 cm/s, then increase to 15 cm/s once the mouse is walking; wait until steady‑state locomotion (consistent running without stumbling or stopping) is achieved, typically 10–30 seconds.

steps.title: Record gait video
steps.instruction: When steady‑state locomotion is achieved, begin video capture for at least five full stride cycles (aim for 5–10 seconds of continuous recording) using the ventral camera that records paw placement of all four limbs simultaneously.

steps.title: Stop treadmill, clean, return mouse
steps.instruction: Stop the belt, open the enclosure, return the mouse to its home cage, then clean the belt surface with 70 % ethanol before the next animal.

steps.title: Analyze video with DigiGait
steps.instruction: Load the recorded video into the DigiGait Analyzer; the software automatically segments individual paw areas across frames and computes gait parameters including stride length, stride frequency, stance width (front and hind), paw area, swing time, stance time, and symmetry indices.

steps.title: Export data and perform statistics
steps.instruction: Export gait parameters for each animal and compare wild‑type versus knockout groups using appropriate statistical tests.
